# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# A REFERENCE ERROR SHAPE, NOT A SERVED FIXTURE -- see error-not-open.json. The --fail argument that
# produces it:
#     fmonero-mock --role wallet --fail transfer=-2:'Invalid address'
# CODE: -2 = WALLET_RPC_ERROR_CODE_WRONG_ADDRESS (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_error_codes.h:35).
# MESSAGE: "Invalid address", set literally by validate_transfer's address branch
#         (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:703-705). THE SAME CODE CARRIES A DIFFERENT MESSAGE a few
#         lines later -- "Address doesn't belong to the wallet" (:710-712) -- and a third at :1064.
#         So -2 is one exit code covering several sentences, and fmonero prints the message VERBATIM
#         rather than substituting its own.
# -2 MAPS TO EXIT 15 invalid_address (§1b.4, §4a), the same exit address::parse gives structurally and
#         the same exit a nettype mismatch gives (§2a.6).
# THIS IS NOT THE SHAPE validate_address RETURNS. `validate_address` answers HTTP 200 with
#         valid: false and NO error object (validate_address-invalid.json); -2 is what the SEND path
#         gets from `transfer`. The two are different wire answers to "is this address usable", which
#         is why §2a.6 validates twice and why exit 15 has both a structural and a daemon source.
# ORDER MATTERS ON THE MONEY PATH (§2a.1): a bad address is caught at step 2 (address::parse, exit 15)
#         or step 6 (validate_address, exit 15) -- both BEFORE the build at step 8 -- so a well-behaved
#         fmonero should rarely see -2 from `transfer` at all. A test that provokes it with --fail is
#         proving the error map, not the refusal order.
